verbalization: Rutin, through its interaction with ATP-binding cassette sub-family G member 1, appears to be a potential modulator of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1-6. This relationship is supported by a chain of targets, where 3'-O-methyltricetin 3-O-alpha-L-rhamnopyranoside, a compound that binds to ATP-binding cassette sub-family G member 1, ultimately targets UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1-6. The evidence suggests a possible mechanism of action where Rutin may influence the activity of this enzyme through its interaction with the intermediate compound, thereby affecting glucuronidation processes. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential role for Rutin in modulating UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1-6, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction and functional significance.
